title: Adjunction for extension by zero
statement:
The functor $j_!$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is left adjoint to
restriction $j^*$ on pro-etale module sheaves.

proof.text: Use the schemes, finite commutative coefficient ring $A$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and functor $j_!M=P_M^\#$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1)--(4), identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, its coefficient sheaf with $A_X|_U$, and restriction with $(j^*N)(V\to U)=N(V\to X)$. Each object over $X$ has at most one map to $U$. These identifications also identify module morphisms and their compositions; thus it suffices to construct the Hom bijection for this localized site.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), construction of the adjunction; specialized to an open immersion using proetale.tex Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero)

proof.text: For a module-sheaf map $\alpha:M\to j^*N$, define $b_\alpha:P_M\to N$ objectwise: it is $\alpha_{V\to U}$ if $V\to X$ factors through $U$, and the unique linear map $0\to N(V)$ otherwise. Here $P_M$ and its restrictions are those of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. For any arrow $a:W\to V$, if $V$ factors through $U$ then $W$ does too and $N(a)\alpha_V=\alpha_W M(a)$ is exactly naturality of $\alpha$ in the localized site. If $V$ does not factor through $U$, both sides of the naturality square have source $P_M(V)=0$. On an object over $U$, $A_X(V)$ acts through its identification with $A_U(V\to U)$, so $\alpha_{V\to U}$ is $A_X(V)$-linear; on every other object the zero-source map is linear. Thus $b_\alpha$ is a morphism of module presheaves.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), construction of the adjunction; specialized to an open immersion using proetale.tex Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero)

proof.text: Conversely, a module-presheaf map $b:P_M\to N$ gives $\alpha_b:M\to j^*N$ by taking its components on objects factoring through $U$. The formula of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] identifies $P_M$ on these objects and arrows with $M$, so the module linearity and naturality of $b$ are precisely those required for $\alpha_b$. The two constructions are inverse: on objects over $U$ both keep the same component, and on all other objects every map from $P_M(V)=0$ is unique. Precomposing by $t:M^\prime\to M$ replaces each nonzero component $b_V$ by $b_Vt_V$, and postcomposing by $s:N\to N^\prime$ replaces it by $s_Vb_V$; zero-source components remain unique. This proves naturality of the resulting presheaf Hom bijection in both variables.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), construction of the adjunction; specialized to an open immersion using proetale.tex Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero)

proof.text: Let $\eta_M:P_M\to P_M^\#$ be the module-sheafification map. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], composition with $\eta_M$ is a bijection from module-sheaf maps $P_M^\#\to N$ to module-presheaf maps $P_M\to N$. Composing with step 3 gives $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*N)$, since $j_!M=P_M^\#$ by [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Write $P_t:P_{M^\prime}\to P_M$ for the presheaf map induced by $t:M^\prime\to M$, and let $\beta:P_M^\#\to N$ be a module-sheaf map. Functoriality of sheafification gives $(j_!t)\eta_{M^\prime}=\eta_M P_t$; for $s:N\to N^\prime$, associativity gives $(s\beta)\eta_M=s(\beta\eta_M)$. Together with step 3 these identities prove naturality of the sheaf Hom bijection. A natural Hom bijection is the defining adjunction, so $j_!\dashv j^*$.

lean.statement: def sfIntrinsicExtensionByZeroAdjunction {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] : sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero j A ⊣ sfIntrinsicOpenRestriction j A
lean.note: Section 1(B): the recorded localized-site adjunction uses proEtaleExtensionByZero on a slice-site category, whereas def-weil-extension-by-zero now records sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero on intrinsic constant-ring modules. Reexport the recorded localized-site interface and construct the canonical intrinsic adjunction by composing the published fixed-scalar localization adjunction with sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence. The right adjoint is sectionwise open restriction transported through that same canonical realization, with no arbitrary map or coefficient identification.
